Coral reefs are in warm seas. A lot of fish and sea animals live there. Coral reefs are beautiful, but they are in danger. We can help: pick up litter and keep our beaches clean. If you are snorkeling or diving, don't touch the reef. Recycle plastic.

Today is Sunday, and it's Mother's Day. This is my breakfast in bed for my mom. My mom likes toast and tea for breakfast. Today she has a rose and some presents, too. My present for my mom is a box of chocolates!

It's night on Ice Island. Hector Frost loves diamonds. "I want the Queen's diamonds, Smith!" Smith goes to town on his skidoo. He takes the diamonds. "Good job, Smith!" BANG! Polly wakes up. "What was that?" The next day, Polly and Mike read the newspaper: "Who has the diamonds?" — "This is a job for the Ice Detectives!" Gizmo finds a red ribbon in the snow. Then they see the skidoo. "Quick! Follow it!"

We can't see the skidoo now. Let's have some ice cream and make a plan. I love strawberry ice cream! — Poor Gizmo! He wants some, too. What do the thieves look like? — One thief has dark hair. The other has light hair. Is he tall or short? Does he have a beard? — I don't know. Woof! It's the man from the skidoo! He's bald! He has no hair! Follow him!

Hi Matt! I'm having a great summer in Spain with the Torres family. Carlos is twelve. He's creative and very smart, and he's patient, too. His sister Nerea is eighteen. She has long, black hair and she's very sporty. Lucia is nine. She's funny but she's very bossy!
This painting has warm colors. There is a lot of red and yellow. It makes me feel happy. That painting has cool colors. There is a lot of blue and green. It makes me feel calm.

Kyle lives in the United Kingdom. His mom has a new husband, and now Kyle has a brother. They play soccer on Saturdays. Lang lives in China. She doesn't have brothers or sisters, but she has good friends and her grandparents play games with her. James lives in the United States. He has three sisters and three brothers. His big sister helps him with his homework.

What's this place? — It's a training camp. We should hide. We can build an igloo! It is nice and warm in here. Smith is working out. He is very strong! We must stay awake, Polly. — Yawn! I am sleepy... Oh no, he isn't here! Look, his shopping bag. These ribbons are like the ribbon in the newspaper!

Emma is a morning person. She always gets up on time and she always makes her bed. She usually has a big breakfast and she often helps in the kitchen. She likes talking with her family before school. She is never late!

Jonas is a soccer player. He must practice every day. He eats meat, vegetables, cereal and fruit. He drinks milk, so his bones and teeth are strong. He always brushes his teeth after meals and before bed, and he goes to the dentist two times a year.

On Thursday at two in the morning I was sleeping. Then the skidoo passed by. — Eat your breakfast, guys! It was going toward the mountains. Why don't we go and look? — But it's Saturday. I play soccer on Saturdays! Come on! We must find the thieves. You're good at soccer and you're good at finding thieves, too! Look at those tracks! Is that the thief? — No, those are wolf tracks. Look! A red ribbon on the tree! This is the right way!
At the sports camp, you can play soccer, swim and dive, and jump on the trampoline. At the theater camp, you can make costumes, sing, dance and act. There is a fantastic show every Friday!

Ben writes music for movies and video games. He's good at playing the piano and he can play the drums. He's good at singing, too. He loves listening to violins and trumpets. Video games are OK, but they aren't his favorite thing.

In mud racing, children run, climb and swim in mud. In cheese rolling, people roll a big cheese down a hill and run to catch it. The winner can eat it! In reindeer racing, people on skis go very fast behind their reindeer. In elephant polo, people play polo on elephants!

Phew! What a climb! The tracks are going north. Let's look at the map. There's a big house on the map. It's called Bollington Hall. Who lives there? There are some children in the forest. — Yes, boss. I think they know something. You must stop those kids! They can't have my diamonds! Smith gets on his skidoo. "Here I come!"

Hello from Egypt! It's very hot, but it's fun. In the desert, there are some big pyramids and an old statue. It has a man's head and a lion's body! Our hotel is on an island in a river. There aren't any cars on the island. Everyone goes by boat.

Hi, I'm Inuk. I live in Greenland. In the winter, we don't see the sun very much and there are big snowstorms. It's very cold, and we go to school by skidoo. In the summer, there are long sunny days. I go kayaking and fishing every day. The summer is great, but it's very short.

Some explorers are in the store. "How much is that jacket?" — "It's five hundred Ice dollars." Can you show us the way to the lake? — Sure! Wow! There are a lot of fish in this lake! Smith pushes Polly into a hole in the ice. "Help!" — "Are you OK?" — "Ye-e-s!" Gizmo chases Smith. "Ouch! Get away from me!" Gizmo has a piece of his pants!

At Crazy Clothing, there are beach clothes, sports clothes and school clothes for boys and girls. Very Cool Sports has soccer shoes, sneakers, hoodies and swimsuits for men, women and children. At Riverside Market, you can buy clothes from around the world, cheese, fruit, toys and books on Saturdays and Sundays.

Sneakers are great for walking in the city, but they are too soft for the mountains. For walking in the mountains, wear strong boots. Dancers move their feet a lot, so their shoes are soft in the middle. For rock climbing, shoes are small and tight.

Bao lives in Vietnam. His family buys food at a floating market. There are a lot of boats, and you can buy fish, rice, coconuts and bananas. Silvia lives in Argentina. She often goes to a bakery after school. Pastries are her favorite food. Lily lives in the United Kingdom. Her family grows fruit in their yard, and their chickens give them eggs.

What happened? — I got the kids. Then a wolf came. Then a polar bear came! Really? A polar bear? We saw this ribbon and we followed the man. He pushed Polly into the lake! — I see. Hector Frost's dog has ribbons like this. And this is Hector Frost's logo! Hector Frost lives at Bollington Hall. Come on, let's go!

Yesterday, we had a welcome party for Sally, a new student at school. Before the party, I went to my friend Mark's house for pizza. There was cool music, but the room was too hot. We talked and played games. Then there was a dancing competition. Mark and Sally got a prize!

In 1620, some settlers went from England to North America on a ship. Their first winter was very cold and they were hungry. In the spring, Native Americans taught them to grow food. In the fall, there was a lot of food, so they had a big dinner to give thanks.

There's a tunnel in the caves. It goes to Bollington Hall. — Cool! Look! A paper. It's a school schedule. How strange! There's a door with a code. — The code is on the schedule! Science is at nine o'clock. Math's at ten-thirty and art's at twelve-forty. — Phew! We did it! Great job, kids! Look at all the lights. Are they having a party?

Sam went on a science trip to a dark cave. There were lots of bats. It was exciting but scary! Luisa went on a history trip. They looked at old buildings and learned about life 400 years ago. Oliver went on a geography trip to a lake. There was a small but beautiful waterfall.

When Tara was a child, her home was in the middle of the desert in Australia. It was far from other children, but it wasn't boring. There were horses on the farm and she had a pet kangaroo! She didn't go to a school building. Her teacher was on the radio in the city, and Tara was on the radio at home.

Kai goes to an international school in Tokyo. He has friends from forty countries and he is learning Japanese. Abi goes to a special school in the mountains in Canada. After her classes, she does winter sports for three hours. Matu lives in his school in Kenya. He never feels lonely because his friends live there, too.

The Queen of Ice Island is at the party. "A dog costume! How funny!" Look! Do you see what I see? — Oh! The diamonds! They are around the dog's neck! My diamonds! How amazing! — Argh! Quick! Catch them! — Help! You are brave and smart children. Thank you! — Just call the Ice Detectives!

In Big Kids, children do their parents' jobs for a week. This week, a boy is a waiter in an expensive restaurant. It's very funny! The Finton Files is an exciting spy story about an American spy in Italy. In Dr. Glock, a scientist and his alien pet go to sea with some sailors. It's fantastic!

The first video games were American. In 1972, there was a tennis game with two white lines and a small white square. In 1989, there was a small Japanese game machine with black and white games. In 2004, there was a game where you play with your whole body. Some sports games are very good exercise!

It's the year 2084 on Future Island. Matt is a time engineer. He works late every night with AL, his robot. Matt, look! A man and a woman have our new THD! — Hey! Stop! That is our time machine! We want to go home, Zeb. — Don't worry, Dot. This machine can help us. They opened a time hole! Quick, AL! Follow them! Hi! I'm Bella. Welcome to the adventure camp! — Thanks! Where are we? And when are we?

We're looking for a man and a woman. They have a time machine. — A time machine? Cool! I love camping, but I want to travel in time! — Are you good at computers? — Yes, I am! Beep! There's a new trace. They went to Africa! — Let's go! Wait! I'm taking my rope and my compass. Safety first! OK, Bella. You can come with us. — Hooray!

Dear Mom, It's my second day at camp. I have new friends from Spain and Mexico. They are teaching me Spanish! Last night there was a big campfire and we sang songs. My tent is cold, but my sleeping bag is warm. Today we are hiking to the wildlife park. Love, Flo

Sam Stone is an adventurer from Canada. He climbed a very high mountain when he was twenty-five. He goes to deserts, mountains and jungles. The jungle is difficult because there are snakes and insects. He sleeps in a tree! Before an adventure, he learns about the plants and animals and he packs a survival kit. He is scared of tall buildings!

Niran lives in Thailand. He camps in a national park with very high mountains and big caves. Kayla lives in the United States. She camps in the desert in the spring because the summer is too hot. Her dad cooks on the campfire. Marco lives in Italy. In the summer, he stays in a small cabin on an island with a volcano. He hikes to the top with his grandpa.

We're in Africa! Look, there are the man and the woman! — They're running away! Rhinos can run fifty kilometers an hour. Cheetahs are faster. They are the fastest animals on land, and they... AL, please be quiet! There is a big rhino behind us! — Oops! Quick! Climb the tree! I can tie my rope to this branch. — Good job, Bella! Hello, little meerkat! Oh no, a cheetah! — Hold on! THD, take us away!

Lulu the koala lived next to a busy road. It was dangerous, and she was sick. Now she lives in a koala reserve. She eats fresh leaves and she sleeps in a big tree. She is safe and healthy. Koalas live longer and are happier in the reserve.

There are about one hundred and sixty kinds of chameleons. Some are smaller than your finger and some are longer than your arm. They have very long tongues and they are good at climbing. Many chameleons change color when they are scared, angry, hot or cold. They eat insects. They catch flies with their tongues!

Where are we now? — This is the lost city of Atlantis. It is under the ocean! How do we get to the control center? — Go straight, then turn left at the mall. Look at this video. The man and the woman are Zeb and Dot Martin. They wanted a space-time chip. A space-time chip is very important for a time machine. The THD has three. — Do you have one, AL? — Yes, I have one more. Shh! A guard! Let's hide behind these newspapers. — I'm hungry. Let's go and eat!

Hi! I live on a very small island. Only six hundred people live here. There is one school and there are two banks, but there are no shopping malls. There is no airport and there are no cars! We go everywhere by bike. To go shopping, we take a boat to a bigger island.

In Barcelona, there is a famous house with funny chimneys on the roof. They look like soldiers! In the park, there is a long bench that looks like a snake. In England, there is a small, quiet village on a river with a lot of little bridges. In Australia, there is a town in the middle of the desert, near a huge red rock.

Luna lives in a cave house in a small town in Spain. Some people think caves are dark, but she loves her home. Kai lives in a very busy city in China. His apartment is on the fortieth floor, and there is a sports center behind it. Sofia lives on a small island in Greece. Her white house is near the harbor, and she likes watching the boats.

These dumplings are delicious! Did you cook them? — No, I didn't. The cook made them. Dot is behind the restaurant. She is looking in a trash can. She wants the old food. Eek! A rat! — It isn't a rat. It's my meerkat! Mm, this soup is really good! — I needed some oil. Ah, that is better! Where did the Martins go? — They took a trash can of old food! Why?
Last May, I played the guitar in a school concert. I was scared and I didn't want to play. Then I went on stage and I was OK. I really liked it! Now I want to be a rock star. — Ben, 12

Anna Brooks sailed alone around the world. Her trip started in November and finished in February. It was often dangerous. There were storms and big waves, and her food was boring. On one very bad day, there was a big storm. She didn't open her presents. A week later, there were no storms. She called her family, opened her presents and laughed.

Welcome to the amusement park! — Thanks. What happened to that ride? Two weird people went on the Space Ride. They sat in a pod and closed the door. Then I saw a flash and I heard a BANG! The pod flew off the ride! — But pods can't fly! Maybe they used the THD for power. — Look! The pod is in the lake. It didn't work. What do Zeb and Dot want? — I don't know. Let's find out!

Hi Gemma! I'm in Hawaii. It's great! On the first day, we went surfing. The ocean was warm, but surfing was difficult. Yesterday it rained, but today it is hot. We played volleyball on the beach. The aquarium was good, and I loved the sea turtles. I'll see you soon! Love, Sarah

At the beach, always wear a T-shirt, a hat and sunblock. Swim between the red and yellow flags. The water is safe there. Never swim near a red flag. It means the water is dangerous. Always surf between the surfing signs and stay with your surfboard.

Ravi went to India and visited the Taj Mahal. An emperor built it for his wife. It took twenty thousand workers! Selin went to Turkey. She stayed near an old castle and she went in a hot-air balloon over strange rocks. Diego went to Peru. He visited an old city in the mountains. People called Incas lived there long ago.

Wow! I always wanted to see a recording studio! — There's nobody here. Help! Help! I'm in the closet! Thank you! A weird man and a weird woman came. They locked me in the closet! — Did they take anything? They recorded some music. Hey, they took the saxophone! A trash can of old food and now a saxophone! What's going on? — We have a trace!

My favorite book is The Secret Diary of Max. It's a comedy with really good cartoons. Max is in middle school and he writes in his diary every day. He has a best friend and a mean little brother. The funniest part happens at Halloween. I read it faster than any other book! — Rosa, 13

On a good day, good things happen. Have you ever won a game? Have you ever helped a friend? Have you ever laughed and laughed? Have you ever eaten a big cake? Have you ever sung a happy song? On a good day, good things happen. Smile and say, "What a day!"

Our machine is ready! — Finally! I can't wait! The saxophone is playing our music. This will work. Don't worry! What's that bright light? Is it a comet? — I don't think so. It's a spaceship! Zeb and Dot are going up! — Quick! Are they astronauts? — Hmm, I wonder. — This is the most amazing adventure ever!

One night in April, a spaceship landed in a field. It was four o'clock in the morning, but the noise and the lights woke Jake up. A door opened and some strange people walked out. They had large heads and small bodies, and they were green. "Am I dreaming?" Jake said. He put on his jeans and ran to the spaceship.

Stars can be different colors. Hot stars are blue, cool stars are red, and the Sun is yellow. The first man in space went there in 1961. The first men walked on the Moon in 1969. In space, astronauts sleep in sleeping bags on the wall. Saturn is farther from the Sun than Jupiter.

In Mali, people play djembe drums. They are made of hard wood and goat skin, and people play them at special celebrations. In Argentina, people play the bandoneón for the tango. It has square boxes with seventy-one buttons, and it is very difficult to play. In Japan, people play the shamisen. It is like a guitar with three strings.

You aren't astronauts. You're aliens! — Yes. We just want to go home to Mars. Our ship broke down. We needed some important things. — Like a saxophone and a trash can of old food? We used the saxophone to call our friends. And we recycle old food. It is our energy! Here is a space-time chip. Please give us back our THD. — Thank you! We'll get home safely now. Now we have to go home, too. — Back to the camp. I'm going to miss you, guys!

Factories, cars and planes send bad gases into the air. This is air pollution, and it makes us sick. We need cleaner energy from the sun, the wind and the water. People also make billions of tons of trash every year. Plastic bottles and bags go into rivers and oceans and kill ocean animals. We have to reduce, reuse and recycle!

The highest waterfall in the world is in Venezuela. Australia is the biggest island and the smallest continent. The Sahara in Africa is the biggest hot desert. The Nile in Africa is the longest river, and the Amazon is a very close second. Mount Fuji is the highest mountain in Japan.
